en.headline: Fire Services clarifies it never requests advance payments for supplies
en.dek: The department issued a statement after reports of a fraudster posing as an officer who asked a clinic to pay a deposit for electric wheelchairs.
body: The Hong Kong Fire Services Department said on Wednesday that it would never ask any shop, medical institution or individual to advance money or buy supplies on its behalf.

The clarification came after a physiotherapy clinic reported that a caller claiming to be a fire station officer had booked several appointments and then asked the clinic to pay a deposit to a designated supplier for 20 electric wheelchairs.
Clinic staff grew suspicious, checked the supplier online and found the name had been used in previous scams. They refused the payment. The booked appointments were not attended.
The department urged the public and businesses to stay alert if they receive similar calls and to report suspected fraud to police.

zh.headline: 消防處澄清絕不會要求商戶墊支代購物品
zh.dek: 部門周三發聲明，指有騙徒假冒消防人員向物理治療診所要求墊付電動輪椅訂金，處方強調絕無此事。
body: 香港消防處周三表示，處方絕對不會要求任何商戶、醫療機構或個人墊支款項，或代為向第三方供應商購買物品。
澄清源於一間物理治療診所接獲自稱消防隊長的來電，對方先預約多個診症時段，其後要求診所向指定供應商墊付20張電動輪椅的訂金。
診所職員起疑，網上查證後發現該供應商名稱曾被用於詐騙，遂拒絕付款。預約的個案最終全部爽約。
消防處呼籲市民及商戶如接到類似電話務必提高警覺，切勿轉帳或代購，並盡快向警方舉報懷疑騙案。
